items.text: Jose Thomas (Head of FS, Adobe, US) states there will always be a need for human advisors because life goals, trade-offs and emotions cannot be automated, but their effectiveness will change: technology will handle research and complexity, while advisors focus on judgment, empathy and guiding clients through decisions that matter most.
items.quote: There will always be a need for human advisors in wealth management because life goals, trade-offs, and emotions can't be automated. What will change is their effectiveness. Technology will handle research and complexity, while advisors focus on judgment, empathy, and guiding clients through decisions that matter most.

items.text: The World Wealth Report states that AI should handle data analysis and pattern recognition collected during client conversations so that relationship managers can focus on life planning, deeper advisory work, and judgment calls requiring human empathy and contextual understanding.
items.quote: Redirect focus: AI handles data analysis and pattern recognition collected during client conversations so that RMs can focus on life planning, deeper advisory work, and judgment calls that require human empathy and contextual understanding.

items.text: The World Wealth Report states the future of wealth management will be defined by personalization at scale, underpinned by empathetic advisory relationships, and engagement models will shift from calendar-driven review cycles to relevance-driven interactions triggered by life transitions, liquidity events and behavioral signals.
items.quote: The future of wealth management will be defined by personalization at scale, underpinned by empathetic advisory relationships... Engagement models will evolve in parallel: life transitions, liquidity events, and behavioral signals will increasingly determine when and how firms interact with clients, replacing calendar-driven review cycles with relevance-driven ones.

items.text: Schwab states it will leverage AI to allow reps to focus on deepening relationships.
items.quote: Leverage AI to allow reps to focus on deepening relationships

items.text: Bank of America CFO Alastair Borthwick states the firm will keep the same number of people plowing into the front end where relationship managers matter (the high-touch piece), with trends being more technology, more intimacy with customers and more built into the process.
items.quote: same number of people, we'll be plowing into the front end, where relationship managers matter, the high- touch piece, which is critically important delivery... the trends will be more technology, more intimacy with the customers

items.text: Morgan Stanley CEO Edward Pick states it is a people business where clients want to make decisions with their financial advisers based on the complexity and singularity of their own financial needs, and that technology can help do a lot of the early work.
items.quote: it's a people business. At some level, if the technology is world-class, folks want to make decisions with their financial advisers based on the complexity and singularity of their own financial needs... that is something that technology can help do a lot of the early work.

items.text: Schwab CEO Rick Wurster states more than 90% of investors prefer human involvement alongside AI technology, and that the combination of people and technology has always been central to Schwab.
items.quote: more than 90% prefer human involvement alongside AI technology. That combination of people and technology has always been central to Schwab and can't be underestimated.

items.text: The World Wealth Report states firms can prioritize services by client segment: for ultra-wealthy clients human specialists such as tax planners and inheritance advisors may be prioritized, while for the digitally-savvy it may increasingly mean digital planning tools, automated insights and AI-driven service access.
items.quote: For ultra-wealthy clients, this may mean prioritizing human specialists such as tax planners, alternative investment desks, and inheritance advisors. For the digitally-savvy, it may increasingly mean digital planning tools, automated insights, and AI-driven service access where the economics of dedicated human specialists do not scale.
